title: [collection-query 10/12] Declare area filters per database in module manifests
body:
**Blocked by:** #1526, #1997
**Model tier:** medium

## Context

Model tier rationale: It composes already-built filter conditions into per-database filter trees and publishes them through an existing schema endpoint, so the mechanism is known, but the trees differ per database and must be checked against real seed data.

"Show everything in the Health area" must give the same answer in every collection, and the answer differs by database. A task has no area of its own; it counts only through its project. A file, a health record or an event may have a project, in which case the project's area counts, or no project, in which case its own area counts. Journal entries and companies only have their own area. If each client assembles these trees itself, the rules drift between clients. This issue puts the rule next to the data, in the module manifest, and publishes it in the schema so a client only substitutes an area id.

What it builds on: the two-hop condition #1363, the emptiness conditions #1526, the Events to Areas relation #1538, and the schema projection of relation properties #1360. It is a dependency of facets (#1759) and related collections (#1839).

Existing code: the manifest of the ten system databases is `backend/packages/data/src/seed/systemDatabasesModuleManifest.ts` (`databases: [{ key, name }, ...]`, validated against the `ModuleManifest` type in `backend/packages/module-registry/src/manifest.ts`). The schema endpoint is `backend/services/semprec-api/src/schemaHandler.ts` (`/api/schema`). Relations: `Tasks.project`, `Events.project` (single), `Files.projects`, `Health records.projects` (many), `Projects.area`; own area: `Files.area`, `Journal.area` (many without inverse), `Health records.area`, `Companies.area` (one-to-one), `Events.area` (added by #1538).

Decision: Tasks use the project path only. A task without a project has no area and must disappear from an area-filtered list. Rationale: this is the behavior the product shows for filtered lists and it avoids a hidden second source of truth for tasks.

Decision: no "only active projects" variant in the filter itself. The filter returns items of deleted projects never (a soft-deleted project is not a live intermediate, see #1363) and does not test a project's status, so items reached through an archived project still match.

Decision (product owner): archived projects are left out of area-filtered lists by default and can be shown with a filter, as elsewhere. Projects therefore get an area filter too, and a client combines it with the Projects quick filters (#1647): the default "Active" chip hides archived projects, the "Archived" and "All" chips show them.

Shared-file ordering: this issue also waits for #1997 because both edit the same registry, manifest, cutover, route matrix or hook files listed in Touches.

## Task

Load `canonical-keys` and `testing`.

1. Extend the `databases[]` entry type in `backend/packages/module-registry/src/manifest.ts` with an optional `areaFilter`: a description of how the database's items are filtered by an area, as data, not code. Shape: a template filter tree in which the area id is a dedicated slot expressed as a typed node (for example `{ "areaValue": true }` in the `value` position), validated by the manifest validator. A database without `areaFilter` is not area-filterable.
2. Declare it in `systemDatabasesModuleManifest.ts`:
   - Tasks: `relation_path_contains { path: ["project", "area"] }` only.
   - Files, Health records and Events: `or( relation_path_contains { path: [<project key>, "area"] }, and( relation_is_empty <project key>, relation_contains <own area key> ) )`, with `<project key>` = `projects` for Files and Health records and `project` for Events, and own area key `area` for all three.
   - Journal and Companies: `relation_contains area`.
   - Projects: `relation_contains area`.
3. Add a helper that expands a declared `areaFilter` for a given area uuid into a real filter tree and validates it with the filter-tree schema from #1363; unit-test that every declaration of the system manifest expands to a tree the compiler accepts for its own database.
4. Expose each database's `areaFilter` in the `/api/schema` response (field `areaFilter`, omitted when absent) so clients substitute the area id themselves.
5. Tests: database-backed checks with seeded Tasks, Files, Health records, Events, Journal, Companies and Projects, covering each acceptance criterion; a schema-handler test for the new field.

## Touches

- backend/packages/module-registry/src/manifest.ts (databases[] entry type and validator)
- backend/packages/data/src/seed/systemDatabasesModuleManifest.ts (databases array)
- backend/packages/data/src/views/areaFilter.ts (new)
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/schemaHandler.ts
- backend/packages/data/src/index.ts (barrel export of the helper)
- backend/packages/data/src/__tests__/areaFilter.test.ts (new)
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/__tests__/schemaHandler.test.ts (area filter field)

## Scope

### In scope

- The declared per-database area filter, its validation, its expansion helper and its publication in `/api/schema`.

### Out of scope

- The conditions themselves: #1363 and #1526.
- The `Events.area` relation: #1538.
- Derived area values on reads: #1595.
- Combining the area filter with other filters in counts and facets: #1759.
- Client-side deep links and default quick-filter choice (owned by the related-collections work in #1839).

## Acceptance criteria

- When Tasks are filtered with the expanded Tasks area filter for area Work, then tasks of Work projects are returned and tasks without a project are not.
- When Files are filtered by area Health, then files of Health projects are returned and so are project-less files whose own area is Health; a file whose project is in another area and whose own area is Health is not.
- When Events are filtered by area Family, then a project-less event with own area Family is returned.
- When Journal or Companies are filtered, then items with the matching own area are returned.
- When Projects are filtered with the expanded Projects area filter for area Work combined with `in status [inProgress, longTerm]` (the default "Active" chip), then an archived Work project is absent; with the area filter alone, it is present.
- `/api/schema` includes `areaFilter` for the seven area-filterable databases (Tasks, Files, Health records, Events, Journal, Companies, Projects) and omits it for the others.
- A manifest whose `areaFilter` references an unknown property or an invalid path is rejected when the manifest is loaded.
